changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7070-no-invented-gantt-date-fields.md`

- names `app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — the console object page. The inline branch becomes `ganttViewOptions`, the sibling of `calendarViewOptions` and `timelineViewOptions`: the declared block spread whole, title floored at `'name'`, no date field invented. - `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — the render branch AND the capability gate. - `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — `generateViewSchema`, the authored `object-view` element route, which bypasses `ListView` entirely.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `c2d86599b` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1478 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2062 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36134451042)

## Contract review

Head-sha: `09d4968100df176d025ce6331b4468bd74b03020`

### ① Derived judgments

**Composition vs spec — agree, no stop.** Read side by side: objectstack `origin/main` 949e99b `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` (docblock :2655-2687 "#15184 ruling B", describe strings :2689-2701) and `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` `effectiveFields` :2921-2954 on the PR head (file untouched by the PR). Step for step: `columns` projects (`Array.isArray(schema.columns) ? … : []`); the FLS drop sits between steps 1 and 2 exactly where the docblock names it (`perms.checkField(…, 'read')`); `hiddenFields` subtracts and can only remove; `fieldOrder` builds an index map, unlisted survivors score `Infinity` so every listed one sorts first, two unlisted compare `Infinity - Infinity` = NaN which ECMAScript's sort treats as +0, and the stable sort keeps their `columns` order — "sorts LAST, keeping its columns-relative order" holds; a listed name with no surviving column orders nothing; nothing is ever added. Empty `columns`: `hasAuthoredColumns` is false (:2956-3130) so the grid derives defaults and `fieldOrder` is never applied to that path — "steps 2 and 3 do not apply" holds. Empty `fieldOrder` `[]`: spec reading (every survivor unlisted, all last in `columns` order) and ListView's `length` greater-than-0 guard produce the same columns order. Duplicates: the spec text is silent; ListView's `Map` takes a duplicated name's LAST index — undeclared, not a disagreement. objectstack's `view-field-order-composition.pin.test.ts` exists on `origin/main` and asserts nothing about empty `fieldOrder` or duplicates.

**The rung.** `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:2704` `fieldOrder: viewDef.fieldOrder ?? listSchema.fieldOrder` vs :2687 `hiddenFields: (viewDef as any).hiddenFields ?? listSchema.hiddenFields`: same operator, same operands, same precedence. `??` is right: `null`/`undefined` on the view falls to the list node, as `hiddenFields` does. An explicit `[]` on the view wins via `??` and ListView then sorts nothing (columns order) — the same shape as `hiddenFields: []` (no subtraction) and the same result the spec gives an empty `fieldOrder`; consistent. The uncast read type-checks: `ViewBody = Record OF string, any` (`utils/viewIdentity.ts:18`). `viewDef = activeView` (:2472) where `activeView` = `viewDraft` merged over `baseView` (:1943-1947), `baseView` found by `activeViewId = resolvedViewId || defaultViewId || views[0]?.id` — named `listViews` entry, default view, runtime switch (`handleViewChange` sets `resolvedViewId`) and an open draft all reach it, and `renderListView`'s deps include `activeView` (:3044); identical to what the `hiddenFields` rung reads. The authored value survives every path to `viewDef`: `viewEntry` is `Object.assign` over the bodies with `id` stamped last (`viewIdentity.ts:127-137`); adapter rows spread `...sv` at :1777 and :913. Other app-shell composers of the schema ListView receives (git grep, 4 non-test sites): `ObjectView.tsx:2979` (this relay), `StudioDesignSurface.tsx:2606` (`...listSchema` spread; its plugin ObjectView at :3446-3470 receives neither `listViews` nor `views`), `ObjectDataPage.tsx:609` (no saved view at all), `InterfaceListPage.tsx:571` — this one resolves `listViews[cfg.sourceView]` (`resolveSourceView`, :288) and hand-projects keys, carrying NEITHER `hiddenFields` NOR `fieldOrder` (0 mentions of either in the file): a symmetric interface-page door, not the `renderListView` asymmetry this card measured. Out of scope; noted below.

**Census.** The `known-gap` row (base :480) is gone; the header sentences at base :22 and :87 are rewritten; the new check `objectui#7516 — the per-view fieldOrder rung is present` (:597-610) has the #7199 (:575) / #7218 (:588) shape — `readsView(writtenAt(key))` with a restore message — plus `listViewReads('fieldOrder')`. Members are still re-derived: `MIRROR_MEMBERS = Object.keys(ListViewMirror.shape)` (:148) from `@object-ui/types/zod` (`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:1391`, spec fields by reference including `fieldOrder`) union `ListViewRuntimeProps` parsed from `objectql.ts`. The `known-gap` kind (:393) and its evidence check (:738) remain, iterating nothing. CONTROL swap to `operations`: it is `node-authored` (:479), a mirror member (`objectql.zod.ts:1522`), not in `RELAYED`, and `ListView.tsx:1590` reads `schema.operations?.export` — a real declared, reader-having absence. Ablation re-run in a scratch `git worktree` at the head (offline `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` from the store, 6.1s): head `pnpm exec vitest run PIN CENSUS` = `Test Files 2 passed (2) · Tests 30 passed (30)`; rung line deleted with `sed` (`grep -c` 1 to 0) = `Tests 5 failed | 25 passed (30)` — census `leaves NO member both unrelayed and undeclared` received `[ 'fieldOrder' ]`, the #7516 named check red (`expected false to be true`), the three FIX pin cases red; both pin CONTROLs and the census CONTROL green; `git checkout --` restored, `git diff HEAD` empty. Matches the dev's `5 failed | 25 passed` exactly. Worktree removed; `/home/user/objectui` untouched (status 0 entries).

**Pins (3 FIX + 2 CONTROL).** Against the base relay (`git show a7df45ff1:…ObjectView.tsx`, rung `grep -c` 0): `Tests 3 failed | 2 passed (5)` — `expected undefined to deeply equal [ 'stage', 'name' ]` (verbatim case) and `expected [ 'owner', 'stage', 'name' ] to deeply equal [ 'stage', 'name' ]` (both override cases): red for the defect, not for a harness reason. Green on head (30/30 above). CONTROL 1 (list node's `fieldOrder` kept when the view authors none) is real — a stomping fix `fieldOrder: viewDef.fieldOrder` fails it — but its `listSchema.fieldOrder` limb is reachable only through the mocked host: in-tree that slot is always undefined on this route (plugin-view fills it from `currentNamedViewConfig` only and app-shell hands no `listViews`); the PR body says so. CONTROL 2 (`undefined ?? undefined`) real. Waiting on `captured.options` as the relay-ran signal is sound.

**The plugin-view finding — true as scoped.** `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:2360` `hiddenFields: activeView?.hiddenFields ?? (schema as any).hiddenFields` vs :2376 `fieldOrder: currentNamedViewConfig?.fieldOrder` (comment :2361-2375, objectui#8980 "view-sourced only"). In-tree `renderListView` hosts (git grep packages/ apps/ non-test): app-shell `ObjectView.tsx:3398,:3441` and `StudioDesignSurface.tsx:3469`, nothing else. App-shell passes `views={mergedViews}`, `activeViewId`, and a `schema={objectViewSchema}` (:3057-3089) with no `listViews`, so plugin-view's `currentNamedViewConfig` is null, `fieldOrder` arrives undefined and the new rung fills it from `viewDef`; for `hiddenFields`, plugin-view's `activeView` (:929, `viewsProp.find` by `activeViewId`) is the same entry app-shell's `viewDef` is, and app-shell overrides it anyway. Studio hands neither `listViews` nor `views`. No reachable in-tree host reads the same authored view differently after this PR. The asymmetry stays latent for an out-of-tree host passing plugin-view `views` carrying `fieldOrder` (it would relay that view's `hiddenFields` and not its `fieldOrder`); the dev's "noted, not filed" leaves it unfiled. Not this card.
